payload.executive_summary: Diffusion and score-based models now produce sharp forecasts, but skill against operational baselines is unmeasured.
payload.background_md:
## Background

Generative models have moved from image synthesis into numerical weather prediction [P1] [P2]. Two families dominate: conditional diffusion models trained directly on reanalysis data [P2], and score-based models applied to radar nowcasting [P3].

- Diffusion models target medium-range ensembles [P2]
- Score-based models target short-horizon nowcasting [P3]
- Latent diffusion has been proposed for seasonal emulation [P1]
payload.method_md:
## Method

This briefing was assembled by searching arXiv for diffusion and score-based generative models applied to weather and climate forecasting [P2].

The ten most relevant candidates were screened against one inclusion criterion: the work proposes or evaluates a generative model for weather or climate forecasting. Papers that do not use observational or reanalysis data were excluded.

comparison.main_result: A latent diffusion emulator is proposed

gaps_and_open_questions.text: None of the abstracts reports a skill score against an operational baseline, so the practical gain over existing systems remains unmeasured.
Evaluation is fragmented across lead times, regions and variables, which makes the three methods hard to compare.

further_reading.text: Start with the medium-range diffusion paper for the clearest description of the method.
